overall: A curious, warm read of someone quietly amazed that a factory now sits in a Navarro County field, at the pace of ordinary talk with no hype. The energy lifts gently as the idea unfolds, drops to its quietest at the honest doubt, and settles lower and more certain on the closing line.

lines.text: Near Barry, in Navarro County, robots now do the heavy lifting on part of a solar farm. A person still has to set each piece down.
lines.intent: open on the surprise, then the human anchor
lines.note: Let the first sentence arrive with mild wonder, weight on robots. The second sentence drops a little and lands plain on person.

lines.text: The project is Tormes Solar, 457 megawatts, built by the contractor SOLV Energy for Matrix Renewables. Building it is expected to support about 450 jobs.
lines.intent: ground the scene in plain facts
lines.note: Matter of fact, unhurried. Say the figures flat with no lift. Weight on jobs at the end.

lines.text: On most solar farms, crews set steel tubes in the field first. Then workers lift heavy glass panels onto them, one by one, hundreds of thousands of them.
lines.intent: set up the usual way so the change can land
lines.note: Easy storytelling pace. A small rise on hundreds of thousands, as if marveling at the scale.

lines.text: So Terabase Energy, a company from Berkeley, California, flipped the order. It parks a factory line right in the field.
lines.note: The brightest line so far. Weight on flipped, then a small smile in the voice on right in the field.

lines.text: On that line, robots fasten the panels onto a long steel tube, called a torque tube. The finished piece is a solar table. For now, the line is optimized for one panel and one tracker, made by First Solar and Nextpower.
lines.note: Walk through it like showing a friend. Weight on torque tube and solar table. The last sentence tapers, a quiet caveat.

lines.text: Then AI-assisted tools check every unit, so a panel in the wrong spot gets caught right away.
lines.note: Interested, not impressed on purpose. Weight on caught.

lines.text: Terabase says one line runs on a two minute cycle. Running around the clock, that is more than 20 megawatts a week.
lines.intent: the scale, attributed to the company
lines.note: Attribute with a slightly dry Terabase says. Then let the number land with real amazement and weight on week.

lines.text: Next, a robot loads the table onto a rover, and the rover drives it out into the field. Tormes is the first site where this version runs with autonomous rovers.
lines.intent: the payoff image and the first-of-its-kind fact
lines.note: Delight at the picture of the rover driving out. The second sentence steadies, weight on first.

lines.text: Here is the fair doubt. This is a proof of concept on a portion of the project. Those speed figures are the company's own, and it says real output depends on the site.
lines.intent: honest turn, the quietest and most important caution
lines.note: Drop clearly below the line before. Say it level and sincere, no lift on the last words. Weight on company's own.

lines.text: The robots also stop short. Workers unload each table and set it on the steel supports waiting in the field.
lines.intent: show where the machine ends and people begin
lines.note: Gentle and observational. Weight on stop short, then plain on the second sentence.

lines.text: Terabase says it is building robots for that last step too.
lines.note: A hint of curiosity, still attributed. Light weight on too.

lines.text: The farm is expected to start running in the first half of 2027. Until then, the robots build the table, and a person sets it down.
lines.intent: land lower and certain, echoing the opening
lines.note: Settle. Date said plainly. The final sentence is the quietest of the close, warm and unhurried, falling on down.
